prose: Having gifts that differ according to the grace given to us, whether prophecy, let us use it in proportion to our faith;

literal: whether service [let us use it] in the service, whether the one teaching [let him be] in the teaching,
prose: or service, let us use it in service; or the one who teaches, in teaching;

literal: whether exhortation, [let him be] in the exhortation, the one giving in simplicity, the one leading in diligence, the one showing mercy in cheerfulness.
prose: if encouragement, in encouragement; the one who gives, let him give with generosity; the one who leads, with diligence; the one who shows mercy, with cheerfulness.

literal: [Let] the love [be] unhypocritical.
prose: Love must be without hypocrisy.

literal: Abhorring the evil [thing], clinging to the good [thing]; in brotherly love toward one another affectionately loving, in honor one another preferring,
prose: Abhor what is evil, cling to what is good; be devoted to one another in brotherly love, outdo one another in showing honor,

literal: in zeal not slothful, in spirit boiling, to the Lord serving,
prose: Do not be slack in zeal, be fervent in spirit, serve the Lord,

literal: In hope rejoicing, in affliction enduring, in prayer persevering,
prose: Rejoice in hope, endure in affliction, persevere in prayer,

literal: In the needs of the saints sharing, hospitality pursuing.
prose: Contribute to the needs of the saints; pursue hospitality.

literal: Bless the ones persecuting [you], bless and do not curse [them].
prose: Bless those who persecute you, bless and do not curse.

literal: [To] rejoice with [those] rejoicing, [to] weep with [those] weeping.
prose: Rejoice with those who rejoice, weep with those who weep.

literal: The same thing toward one another thinking, not the high things thinking, but to the lowly being carried along with.
prose: Being of the same mind toward one another; not setting your minds on high things, but being carried along with the lowly.

literal: To no one evil for evil rendering [be ye], taking-thought-for good-things in-the-sight of-all men.
prose: Render to no one evil for evil; take thought for what is good in the sight of all people.

literal: If [it is] possible, that [which is] from you, with all men being at peace.
prose: If possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with all men.

literal: Not yourselves avenging, beloved, but give place to the wrath, for it has been written, 'To Me [belongs] vengeance, I will repay,' says the Lord.
prose: Beloved, do not avenge yourselves, but leave room for wrath, for it is written: 'Vengeance belongs to Me; I will repay,' says the Lord.

literal: For this, doing [it], you will heap coals of fire upon the head of him.
prose: For in doing this, you will heap coals of fire on his head.

literal: Do not be overcome by the evil, but overcome the evil in the good.
prose: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.

literal: Every soul to the governing authorities let it be subjected; for not is authority except [it be] by God, and the [authorities] that are, by God having been ordained they are.
prose: Let every soul be subject to the governing authorities, for there is no authority except from God, and the authorities that exist have been established by God.

literal: So-that the [one] resisting the authority, the [one] of God, to [his] ordinance has opposed, and the [ones] having opposed [it] for themselves judgment will receive.
prose: So then, the one who resists authority has opposed God's ordinance, and those who have opposed it will receive judgment for themselves.

literal: For the rulers are not a fear to the good work, but to the bad [work].
prose: For rulers are not a terror to good conduct, but to bad.

literal: Of God for a servant he is to you for the good. But if the evil you do, be afraid; for not in vain the sword he bears; for of God a servant he is, an avenger unto wrath to the one doing the evil.
prose: For he is God's servant to you for good. But if you do evil, be afraid, for he does not bear the sword in vain; for he is God's servant, an avenger to execute wrath on the one who does evil.

literal: Therefore [there is] necessity to be subject, not only on account of the wrath but also on account of the conscience,
prose: Therefore it is necessary to be subject, not only because of wrath but also because of conscience,

literal: On account of this for also taxes you pay; for ministers of God they are, unto this very thing attending continually.
prose: For because of this you also pay taxes; for they are God's servants, attending continually to this very thing.

literal: To the one [owing] the tax, the tax; to the one [owing] the toll, the toll; to the one [owing] the fear, the fear; to the one [owing] the honor, the honor.
prose: Tax to whom tax is due, toll to whom toll is due, fear to whom fear is due, honor to whom honor is due.

literal: To no one owe nothing, except [this,] the [one] another [i.e. one another] to love; for the [one] loving the other [i.e. neighbor] has fulfilled law.
prose: Owe no one anything, except to love one another; for the one who loves his neighbor has fulfilled the law.

literal: For the [commandment], 'You shall not commit adultery, You shall not murder, You shall not steal,' 'You shall not covet,' and if there is any other commandment, in this word it is summed up, [namely] in [the commandment], 'You shall love the neighbor of you as yourself.'
prose: For the commandments, 'You shall not commit adultery, You shall not murder, You shall not steal, You shall not covet,' and if there is any other commandment, are summed up in this word: 'You shall love your neighbor as yourself.'

literal: The love to-the neighbor evil not works; [the] fulfillment, therefore, of-law [is] the love.
prose: Love does no wrong to one's neighbor; love, then, is the fulfillment of the law.

literal: And this, knowing the time, that [it is] already an hour for you out of sleep to be roused; for now nearer of us [is] the salvation than when we believed.
prose: And do this, knowing the time, that it is already the hour for you to be roused out of sleep; for now our salvation is nearer than when we believed.

literal: The night has advanced, and the day has drawn near.
prose: The night is far gone, and the day has drawn near.

literal: As in [the] day, properly let-us-walk, not in revelings and drunkennesses, not in beds and acts-of-licentiousness, not in strife and jealousy.
prose: Let us walk properly, as in the daytime, not in reveling and drunkenness, not in sexual immorality and licentiousness, not in strife and jealousy.

literal: But put on [yourselves with] the Lord Jesus Christ, and of the flesh make no forethought, unto desires.
prose: But put on the Lord Jesus Christ, and make no provision for the flesh, to satisfy its desires.

literal: But the one being weak in the faith receive you, not unto disputes of opinions.
prose: Accept the one who is weak in faith, not for disputes over opinions.

literal: One indeed believes to eat all things, but the one being weak eats vegetables.
prose: One person believes he may eat anything, while the one who is weak eats only vegetables.

literal: The one eating, let him not despise the one not eating; and the one not eating, let him not judge the one eating; for God received him.
prose: Let the one who eats not despise the one who abstains, and let the one who abstains not judge the one who eats; for God has accepted him.

literal: You, who are you, the one judging another's household-servant? To the [his] own lord he stands or he falls. But he will be made to stand, for [the] Lord is able to make him stand.
prose: Who are you to judge another's servant? To his own lord he stands or falls. But he will stand, for the Lord is able to make him stand.

literal: For one [man] on the one hand judges day above day, but another judges every day [alike].
prose: For one person judges one day above another, while another judges every day [alike].

literal: The one regarding the day, regards [it] for [the] Lord. And the one eating eats to [the] Lord, for he gives thanks to [the] God; and the one not eating does not eat to [the] Lord, and he gives thanks to [the] God.
prose: He who regards the day, regards it for the Lord. And he who eats, eats to the Lord, for he gives thanks to God; and he who does not eat, does not eat to the Lord, and he gives thanks to God.

literal: For no one of us to himself lives, and no one to himself dies;
prose: For none of us lives for himself, and none dies for himself;

literal: For if indeed we live, to the Lord we live, and if we die, to the Lord we die, whether then we live or whether we die, of the Lord we are.
prose: For if we live, we live to the Lord, and if we die, we die to the Lord; whether we live, then, or whether we die, we belong to the Lord.

literal: For unto this [end] Christ died and lived, so that both of [the] dead and of [the] living he might be lord.
prose: For this reason Christ died and lived again, so that he might be lord both of the dead and of the living.

literal: For all we will stand before the judgment-seat of God;
prose: For we will all stand before the judgment seat of God.

literal: For it has been written, "Live I," says Lord, "that to me will bend every knee, and every tongue will confess to God."
prose: For it is written: 'As I live, says the Lord, every knee will bow to me, and every tongue will confess to God.'

literal: So then each of us concerning himself an account will give [to God].
prose: So then each of us will give an account of himself to God.

literal: But judge this rather: not to put a stumbling block before the brother, or a cause-of-stumbling [to put before the brother].
prose: But rather judge this: not to put a stumbling block or a hindrance in front of your brother.

literal: I know and have been persuaded in the Lord Jesus that nothing [is] unclean through itself, except to-the [one] reckoning something [to-be] unclean, to-that-one [it is] unclean.
prose: I know and am persuaded in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean in itself; except to the one who reckons something to be unclean — to that one it is unclean.

literal: For if because of food your brother is grieved, no longer according to love are you walking. Not by the food of you that one destroy, for whom Christ died.
prose: For if your brother is grieved because of food, you are no longer walking according to love. Do not by your food destroy that one for whom Christ died.

literal: Not therefore let your good be blasphemed.
prose: Therefore do not let your good be slandered.

literal: For not is the kingdom of God food and drink, but righteousness and peace and joy in [the] Holy Spirit;
prose: For the kingdom of God is not eating and drinking, but righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit;

literal: For the one serving Christ in this [is] well-pleasing to God and approved to men.
prose: For the one who serves Christ in this way is pleasing to God and approved by men.

literal: So then, the things of peace let us pursue, and the things of the building up that [is] toward one another.
prose: So then, let us pursue the things that make for peace and the things that build up one another.

literal: Not for the sake of food tear down the work of God. All things [are] indeed clean, but [it is] evil for the man, [namely] for the one eating through [a] stumbling.
prose: Do not tear down the work of God for the sake of food. Everything is indeed clean, but it is evil for the man who eats through stumbling.

literal: [It is] good [the] not to eat meat nor to drink wine, nor [anything] by which your brother stumbles;
prose: It is good not to eat meat or drink wine or do anything by which your brother stumbles.

literal: You, the faith which you have, according to yourself have [it] before God.
prose: The faith that you have, keep to yourself before God.

literal: But the one doubting, if he should eat, has been condemned, because [it is] not from faith; but everything that [is] not from faith is sin.
prose: But the one who doubts is condemned if he eats, because it is not from faith; and whatever is not from faith is sin.

literal: But we ought, we the strong [ones], the weaknesses of the weak [ones] to bear, and not to ourselves to please.
prose: But we who are strong ought to bear the weaknesses of the weak, and not to please ourselves.

literal: Let each of us please the neighbor unto the good, toward building up.
prose: Let each of us please his neighbor for his good, for the building up of others.

literal: For even the Christ did not please himself; but just as it has been written, 'The reproaches of the ones reproaching you fell upon me.'
prose: For even Christ did not please himself; but, as it is written, 'The reproaches of those who reproached you fell upon me.'

literal: For as many things as were written beforehand, [all things] were written for our instruction, in order that through the patience and through the comfort of the scriptures we might have the hope.
prose: For whatever was written beforehand was written for our instruction, so that through the patience and through the comfort of the scriptures we might have hope.

literal: Now the God of endurance and of encouragement, may he grant to you the same thing to think among one another according to Christ Jesus,
prose: Now may the God of endurance and encouragement grant you to be of the same mind with one another according to Christ Jesus,

literal: in order that with one accord, in one mouth, you may glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
prose: so that with one accord, with one mouth, you may glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.

literal: Therefore welcome one another, just as also [the] Christ welcomed us, to [the] glory of [the] God.
prose: Therefore welcome one another, just as Christ also welcomed us, to the glory of God.

literal: For I say [that] Christ to have become a servant of circumcision, on behalf of the truth of God, for the confirming of the promises of the fathers,
prose: For I say that Christ has become a servant of the circumcision for the sake of God's truth, in order to confirm the promises given to the fathers,

literal: and the Gentiles, [became servants, understood] on behalf of mercy, to glorify God; just as it has been written, "Because of this, I will confess to you among [the] Gentiles, and to [the] name of you I will sing."
prose: and that the Gentiles might glorify God for his mercy; as it is written: "Because of this, I will confess to you among the Gentiles, and I will sing praise to your name."

literal: And again he says, "Be glad, Gentiles, with the people of him."
prose: And again he says, "Rejoice, O Gentiles, with his people."

literal: And again: Praise, all the Gentiles, the Lord, and let extol him all the peoples.
prose: And again: Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles, and let all the peoples extol him.

literal: Upon him [the] Gentiles will hope.
prose: In him the Gentiles will hope.

literal: Now the God of hope may he fill you with all joy and peace in the believing, unto the abounding of you in hope, in power of Holy Spirit.
prose: May the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, so that you may abound in hope by the power of the Holy Spirit.

literal: But I have been persuaded, my brothers of mine, I myself also, concerning you, that you yourselves are full of goodness, having been filled with all the knowledge, being able also to instruct one another.
prose: But I myself am also convinced concerning you, my brothers, that you yourselves are full of goodness, filled with all knowledge, and able also to instruct one another.

literal: But more boldly I wrote to you in part, as reminding you again, because of the grace, the [grace] given to me from God
prose: But I have written to you rather boldly in part, as reminding you again, because of the grace given to me by God

literal: unto the [for] me to be a minister of Christ Jesus unto the Gentiles, serving as priest the gospel of God, in order that the offering of the Gentiles might become well-accepted, having been sanctified in [the] Holy Spirit.
prose: that I should be a minister of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles, serving as a priest the gospel of God, so that the offering of the Gentiles might become acceptable, sanctified by the Holy Spirit.

literal: I have therefore [the] boast in Christ Jesus, the things toward God.
prose: I therefore have [this] boast in Christ Jesus regarding the things pertaining to God.

literal: For I will not dare to speak anything of [the things] which Christ did not work through me, into [the] obedience of [the] Gentiles, by word and by deed,
prose: For I will not dare to speak of anything except what Christ accomplished through me to bring about the obedience of the Gentiles, in word and deed,

literal: in [the] power of signs and wonders, in [the] power of [the] Spirit [Holy]; so-that I, from Jerusalem and in-a-circle as-far-as the Illyricum, [am] having-fulfilled the gospel of-the Christ,
prose: by the power of signs and wonders, by the power of the [Holy] Spirit; so that from Jerusalem and round about as far as Illyricum I have fully preached the gospel of Christ,

literal: but thus making-it-my-ambition to-preach-the-gospel not where Christ was-named, in-order-that not upon another's foundation I-might-build,
prose: but making it my ambition in this way to preach the gospel not where Christ had already been named, so that I might not build on another's foundation,

literal: but as it-has-been-written, 'They-shall-see, to-whom it-was-not-announced concerning him, and they who have-not-heard shall-understand.'
prose: but, as it is written, 'They to whom no report of him came shall see, and they who have not heard shall understand.'

literal: Therefore also I was being hindered the many times from the coming to you;
prose: That is also why I was so often hindered from coming to you.

literal: but now, no longer having a place in these regions, and having a longing of coming to you from sufficient years,
prose: but now, having no longer any room in these regions, and having a longing to come to you for many years,

literal: whenever I might journey into Spain—for I hope, journeying through, to see you and to be sent forward there by you, if of you first I might be filled in part—
prose: whenever I journey to Spain—for I hope to see you as I pass through, and to be sent on my way there by you, if first I may be somewhat filled with your company—

literal: But now I journey into Jerusalem, ministering to the saints.
prose: But now I am going to Jerusalem, ministering to the saints.

literal: For they were well-pleased—Macedonia and Achaia—to make a certain contribution unto the poor of the saints, of those in Jerusalem.
prose: For Macedonia and Achaia were pleased to make some contribution for the poor among the saints who are in Jerusalem.

literal: For they were well pleased, and debtors they are of them; for if the Gentiles shared in their spiritual things, they owe [it], also in the fleshly things, to minister to them.
prose: For they were pleased to do so, and indeed they are their debtors; for if the Gentiles have shared in their spiritual things, they ought also to minister to them in material things.

literal: This therefore, having completed [it], and having sealed to them this fruit, I will go away through you into Spain.
prose: So when I have completed this and have sealed to them this fruit, I will go on through you into Spain.

literal: But I know that, coming to you, I will come in [the] fullness of [the] blessing of Christ.
prose: And I know that when I come to you, I will come in the fullness of Christ's blessing.

literal: I urge now you, [, brothers, ], through the Lord of us Jesus Christ and through the love of the Spirit, to strive-together with me in the prayers on behalf of me toward God,
prose: Now I urge you, brothers, through our Lord Jesus Christ and through the love of the Spirit, to strive together with me in your prayers on my behalf to God,

literal: in order that I might be rescued from the ones disobeying in Judea, and the service of me, the one for Jerusalem, might become acceptable to the saints,
prose: that I may be rescued from those who are disobedient in Judea, and that my service for Jerusalem may become acceptable to the saints,

literal: in order that in joy having come to you through the will of God I might rest-together-with you.
prose: so that, coming to you in joy by the will of God, I may rest together with you.

literal: Now the God of peace [be] with all of you. Amen.
prose: Now the God of peace be with all of you. Amen.

literal: I commend now to you Phoebe the sister of us, being [also] a servant of the church, the one in Cenchreae,
prose: I commend to you Phoebe our sister, who is also a servant of the church that is in Cenchreae,

literal: in order that you may receive her in [the] Lord worthily of the saints, and may stand by her in whatever matter she may have need of you, for she herself also became a patroness of many, and of me myself.
prose: so that you may receive her in the Lord in a manner worthy of the saints, and may assist her in whatever matter she may have need of you; for she herself has also become a patron of many, and of me myself.

literal: Greet Prisca and Aquila, the fellow-workers of-me in Christ Jesus,
prose: Greet Prisca and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus,

literal: who-indeed on-behalf-of the soul of-me their-own neck laid-under, to whom not I alone give-thanks but also all the churches of-the Gentiles,
prose: who risked their own necks for my life, to whom not only I give thanks, but also all the churches of the Gentiles,

literal: Greet Epaenetus the beloved of-me, who is firstfruit of-the Asia unto Christ; and the according-to house of-them church.
prose: Greet my beloved Epaenetus, who is the firstfruit of Asia for Christ; and greet the church in their house.

literal: Greet Mary, who many things labored for you.
prose: Greet Mary, who has worked hard for you.

literal: Greet Andronicus and Junia, the relatives of me and fellow-prisoners of me, who are outstanding among the apostles, who also have come to be in Christ before me.
prose: Greet Andronicus and Junia, my relatives and fellow prisoners, who are outstanding among the apostles, and who were in Christ before me.

literal: Greet Ampliatus, the beloved of me in [the] Lord.
prose: Greet Ampliatus, my beloved in the Lord.

literal: Greet Urbanus the fellow-worker of-us in Christ and Stachys the beloved of-me.
prose: Greet Urbanus, our fellow worker in Christ, and Stachys, my beloved.

literal: Greet Apelles, the approved [one], in Christ. Greet the [ones] from the [household] of Aristobulus.
prose: Greet Apelles, the one approved in Christ. Greet those who belong to the household of Aristobulus.

literal: Greet Herodion, the relative of me. Greet the ones from those of Narcissus, the ones being in [the] Lord.
prose: Greet Herodion, my relative. Greet those of Narcissus's household who are in the Lord.

literal: Greet Tryphaena and Tryphosa, the ones laboring in [the] Lord. Greet Persis, the beloved [one], who labored many things in [the] Lord.
prose: Greet Tryphaena and Tryphosa, who have worked hard in the Lord. Greet Persis, the beloved, who has labored much in the Lord.

literal: Greet Rufus the chosen [one] in [the] Lord, and the mother of him and of me.
prose: Greet Rufus, who is chosen in the Lord, and his mother and mine.

literal: Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers with them.
prose: Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers who are with them.

literal: Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and the sister of him, and Olympas, and the [ones] with them all saints.
prose: Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas, and all the saints with them.

literal: Greet one another with a holy kiss. Greet you all the churches of the Christ.
prose: Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the churches of Christ greet you.

literal: Now I urge you, brothers, to watch out for the [ones] the divisions and the offenses contrary to the teaching which you learned making, and turn away from them.
prose: Now I urge you, brothers, to watch out for those causing the divisions and the offenses contrary to the teaching which you learned, and turn away from them.

literal: For such ones to our Lord Christ not do they serve, but to their own belly, and through the fine-speaking and blessing-speech they deceive the hearts of the guileless ones.
prose: For such people do not serve our Lord Christ, but their own belly, and through smooth talk and flattering speech they deceive the hearts of the guileless.

literal: For your obedience has arrived to all [people];
prose: For your obedience has reached everyone.

literal: And the God of peace will crush Satan under your feet in speed. The grace of our Lord Jesus [be] with you.
prose: And the God of peace will crush Satan under your feet shortly. The grace of our Lord Jesus be with you.

literal: Greets you Timothy the fellow worker [of me], and Lucius and Jason and Sosipater, the kinsmen of me.
prose: Timothy my fellow worker greets you, and so do Lucius and Jason and Sosipater, my kinsmen.

literal: I greet you, I, Tertius, the one who wrote the letter, in [the] Lord.
prose: I, Tertius, who wrote this letter, greet you in the Lord.

literal: Greets you Erastus the treasurer of the city, and Quartus the brother.
prose: Erastus, the city treasurer, greets you, and Quartus the brother.

literal: Now to the [one] being able to establish you according to the gospel of me and the proclamation of Jesus Christ, according to [the] revelation of [the] mystery having been kept silent in times eternal,
prose: Now to Him who is able to establish you according to my gospel and the proclamation of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the mystery kept silent in eternal times,

literal: but now having been made manifest, and through prophetic writings, according to [the] command of the eternal God, unto obedience of faith, unto all the nations, having been made known
prose: but now made manifest, and through the prophetic writings made known, according to the command of the eternal God, for obedience of faith among all the nations

literal: to [the] only wise God, through Jesus Christ, [to whom be] the glory unto the ages; Amen.
prose: to the only wise God, through Jesus Christ, to whom be the glory forever. Amen.
